rules.title: Cap on up-front payments at start of tenancy (lessor or lessor's agent)
rules.requirement: At or before move-in, a landlord or the landlord's agent (such as a broker the landlord hired) can only require first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit of no more than one month's rent, and the cost of buying and installing a new lock and key. They cannot require any other up-front fee, such as an application fee or a broker fee paid to the landlord's agent.
rules.key_value: First month + last month + security deposit (≤1 month) + lock/key cost; nothing else
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential leases and tenancies in Massachusetts; the version effective August 1, 2025 also covers agents of the lessor.
rules.exemptions: Leases or rentals of 100 days or less for vacation or recreational purposes (subsection 9).
rules.quoted_span: (b) At or prior to the commencement of any tenancy, no lessor or agent of the lessor may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay, to the lessor or to an agent of the lessor, any amount in excess of the following:

rules.title: Security deposit capped at one month's rent
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot charge a security deposit of more than one month's rent, either at move-in or at any time later in the tenancy. If state regulations allow a fee instead of a deposit, the fee plus any deposit together cannot add up to more than one month's rent.
rules.exemptions: Vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less.
rules.quoted_span: a security deposit equal to the first month's rent provided that such security deposit is deposited as required by subsection (3)
rules.penalty: If the landlord tries to enforce lease terms that conflict with this section, they lose the right to keep any part of the deposit (§ 15B(6)(c)).

rules.title: Deposit must be held in a separate Massachusetts bank account, with receipts and a statement of condition
rules.requirement: The landlord must keep your deposit in a separate interest-bearing account at a bank in Massachusetts. Within 30 days they must give you a receipt showing the bank, account number and amount. They must also give you a written statement of the unit's condition within 10 days of move-in (or when you pay the deposit, if later). If the landlord does not put the deposit in such an account, you are entitled to get it back right away.
rules.key_value: Separate interest-bearing MA bank account; bank receipt within 30 days; condition statement within 10 days
rules.coverage_conditions: Any residential lessor who accepts a security deposit in Massachusetts.
rules.exemptions: Vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less.
rules.quoted_span: Any security deposit received by such lessor shall be held in a separate, interest-bearing account in a bank, located within the commonwealth
rules.penalty: Tenant is entitled to immediate return of the deposit. If the deposit is not held in a proper account, the landlord loses the right to keep any of it, and the tenant can recover three times the deposit plus 5% interest, court costs and attorney's fees (§ 15B(6)(a), (7)).

rules.title: Interest on security deposits and last month's rent
rules.requirement: Your landlord must pay you interest every year on your security deposit (if they hold it for a year or more) and on any last month's rent you paid in advance. The rate is 5% a year, or the lower rate the bank actually paid. If you do not get the interest or a notice within 30 days after the end of each tenancy year, you may deduct it from your next rent payment.
rules.key_value: 5% per year or the lower actual bank rate, paid each year
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential lessors holding a security deposit for one year or longer, or holding last month's rent paid in advance.
rules.exemptions: Vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less.
rules.quoted_span: A lessor of residential real property who holds a security deposit pursuant to this section for a period of one year or longer from the commencement of the term of the tenancy shall, beginning with the first day of the tenancy, pay interest at the rate of five per cent per year
rules.penalty: If interest on last month's rent is not paid within 30 days after the tenancy ends, the tenant can recover three times the interest owed plus court costs and attorney's fees.

rules.title: Return of security deposit within 30 days, with itemized deductions
rules.requirement: The landlord must return your deposit, plus interest, within 30 days after your tenancy ends. They may only deduct unpaid rent or water charges, certain tax escalation charges, and reasonable repair costs for damage beyond normal wear and tear. For damage deductions, they must give you a sworn, itemized list with written proof of the costs within those same 30 days.
rules.key_value: Return within 30 days; only listed deductions allowed; treble damages for violations
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential tenancies in Massachusetts where a security deposit was collected.
rules.exemptions: Vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less.
rules.quoted_span: The lessor shall, within thirty days after the termination of occupancy under a tenancy-at-will or the end of the tenancy as specified in a valid written lease agreement, return to the tenant the security deposit or any balance thereof;
rules.penalty: The landlord loses the right to keep any part of the deposit. The tenant can recover three times the deposit or balance owed, plus 5% interest, court costs and reasonable attorney's fees (§ 15B(7)).

notes: The source is the official text of M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B. The page shows two versions of the § 15B(1)(b) introduction: one in effect until August 1, 2025, and one amended by St. 2025, c. 9, §§ 54-55 starting August 1, 2025. The amended version adds 'agent of the lessor', which shifts broker fees away from tenants. Only the amended version is recorded, because it is the one in force on 2026-10-01. The fee-in-lieu-of-deposit option in (1)(b)(iii) depends on regulations from the Executive Office of Housing and Livable Communities. This document does not say whether those regulations have been issued, so the option is mentioned inside the deposit-cap record, not as a separate rule. Several parts of the section are out of scope and were left out: entry rules (1)(a), the 30-day late-fee bar (1)(c), and the transfer of deposits to a new owner (5)/(7A). The transfer rules relate to deposits but are procedural. The only exemption, vacation rentals of 100 days or less, never applies to ordinary apartments, so no exemption tests were recorded. The document gives no effective dates for the provisions that were not amended.
